comment: What the « LGV France » dataset is made of. bbox: south, west, north, east (degrees), the whole of metropolitan France. Tiles of tileDeg degrees are asked one by one for the high-speed tracks. The approaches are the classic lines that take the trains from the end of a high-speed line into a city-centre terminal: a corridor of waypoints (lat, lon), the rails within radiusM of it, and every rail within stationRadiusM of the terminal. Waypoints are the stations of the SNCF list along the way, plus a few places where the line bends between two stations. lines: the lines published, each made of the ways of the OSM relations listed (type=route, route=railway|tracks: the whole line, its « voie 1 / voie 2 » and section relations), in order of precedence; refs and names of those relations are too unsteady to go by (« 752 000 » with a space, « LN2 », none at all, three LGV under one RFN code). A high-speed way in none of them takes the line of a neighbouring section, else « autres ». subways: the metro of a city the dataset reaches, every railway=subway track in its box (south, west, north, east) but its depots, each line named by its routes (route=subway, by ref).

approaches.name: Raccordement de Marseille Saint-Charles
approaches.comment: From the bifurcation des Tuileries, where the LGV Méditerranée joins the Paris–Marseille line in the north of Marseille (Saint-Louis), down to Saint-Charles along that line (7.4 km): the waypoints follow its curve through Les Aygalades and Saint-Barthélemy, about a kilometre apart.

approaches.name: Raccordement de Lyon Part-Dieu par le sud
approaches.comment: From Saint-Quentin-Fallavier past the junction of Grenay (where the raccordement of the LGV Rhône-Alpes joins the Lyon–Grenoble line) along that line to Saint-Priest and Vénissieux, then the Paris–Marseille line north to Lyon-Guillotière and its raccordement to Part-Dieu. Waypoints follow the track about a kilometre apart where it curves (it runs 800 m north of the straight line Saint-Quentin – Saint-Priest, and 600 m west of the straight line Vénissieux – Guillotière), through the Guillotière triangle to Part-Dieu.

approaches.name: Raccordement de Lyon Part-Dieu par le nord
approaches.comment: From the junction where the LGV Sud-Est meets the Lyon–Bourg line north of Montanay, down that line: Sathonay-Rillieux, Lyon Saint-Clair, Lyon Part-Dieu. The waypoints are sampled every 700 m along the way a train runs (the shortest way along the rails of OpenStreetMap, 18 km): four waypoints strayed up to 4 km from the track and left Part-Dieu cut off from the north.

approaches.name: Raccordement de Paris Gare de Lyon
approaches.comment: From the start of the LGV Sud-Est at Lieusaint along the Paris–Marseille line: Lieusaint-Moissy, Combs-la-Ville, Brunoy, Montgeron, Villeneuve-Saint-Georges, Maisons-Alfort, Paris Gare de Lyon. The waypoints are sampled every 700 m along the way a train runs (the shortest way along the rails of OpenStreetMap between the two ends, 30.6 km): seven waypoints strayed up to 740 m from the track and left the approach in twelve pieces. The terminal disc is 1 km: the platforms of Gare de Lyon reach 800 m from its head.

regions.name: Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
regions.comment: The first region taken whole, around Marseille: the classic lines a TER or an Intercités runs on. Each line is its OSM relation (route=railway), main or branch by the usage of its tracks.

subways.name: Métro de Paris
subways.comment: Reached by the raccordement of Paris Gare de Lyon. The box holds the sixteen lines, line 14 down to Orly airport included; Orlyval and CDGVAL are not railway=subway.

subways.name: Métro de Lyon
subways.comment: Reached by the two raccordements of Lyon Part-Dieu. Lines A to D; the funiculars are railway=funicular.

subways.name: Métro de Marseille
subways.comment: Inside the region Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, reached by the raccordement of Marseille Saint-Charles.

subways.name: Métro de Lille
subways.comment: On the LGV Nord (Lille Europe, Lille Flandres): the two VAL lines, Saint-Philibert to 4 Cantons and Lille to Tourcoing.
